question: In a Bloomberg SDE Intern technical round, the candidate was asked to implement their own resizable list class with O(1) indexed access that can allocate new memory and change size dynamically. The interviewer then asked how much extra memory to allocate when growing, and why.
lookingFor: Implementing a dynamic array with correct capacity vs size management
Reasoned choice of growth factor (memory vs copy cost)
Edge cases: bounds checks, shrinking, large sizes
followUps: Prove that append is amortized O(1) with doubling.
Why shrink at 1/4 and not 1/2 full?
What is the cost of insert at the beginning or middle?
How does this differ from a linked list in access time and cache behaviour?
